cards.title: Pipeline runs as typed session jobs: one runner, keyed lesson, no silent fails
acceptance: case 1: text engine stub throws on POST /api/practice {topic:'linear-one-step'} -> getSession().jobs.practice.phase === 'failed' with a desk-worded error (no 'Error:' prefix, no stack); a second POST with a working stub -> jobs.practice.phase === 'done' and practice.items.length === 6 (tools/desk-jobs-rules-test.cjs, node:test, engines stubbed at lib/engines/text.ts)

cards.body:
## Summary
The eight homework routes each run a 5-60 s model pipeline inside the HTTP request and report what happened through one free-text `status` string that no TV screen renders. Replace that with a typed `jobs` record in the session (kind -> running | done | failed, startedAt, a desk-worded error) written by one `runJob()` wrapper every route uses, with a one-in-flight guard per kind and the lesson pick keyed to the hint it belongs to.

## Description
Today the lifecycle of a pipeline run is re-implemented per route: 21 status dispatches and 6 copies of the same try/catch, one route (hint) with none, and the lesson pick fire-and-forget. The TV then infers state from a scatter of booleans (reading, noLesson, a local busy, lesson === null) that have no 'failed' branch, so every failure is silent on the stage: a failed practice set leaves Topics saying 'nothing to press' forever, a failed or malformed lesson pick leaves 'Finding the lesson...' forever, a thrown hint does nothing at all. The same missing seam causes counting bugs: a double Select runs two hints, and 'Still stuck' counts as two hints because hint.set and hint.stage both increment. And because lesson.set is not keyed, the previous item's lesson stays live on a new hint.

`lib/desk/job.ts` exports `runJob(kind, work)` that dispatches job start, returns 409 if that kind is already running, awaits the pipeline, dispatches done or failed with a sentence the desk would say (never String(e)), and still writes `status` so the bench bar and phone keep working. The lesson pick runs as its own `lesson` job carrying the hint key; hint.set clears lesson/noLesson; lesson.set for another key is dropped; a failed pick sets noLesson. Store load() demotes a persisted running job. The TV reads `s.jobs`: Topics shows the failure in the caption slot and Select retries; the Hint screen's lesson button resolves.

Contract (session shape, API responses): consumers are desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx, desk/src/tv/screens.tsx, desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx (status at :231, :334 kept), session.json via store load(), and tools/maths-rules-test.cjs:112 (practice response keys, kept). The Linga routes and LingaTV are not touched. A TV surface changes, so the overlay's Playwright capture applies (On Air: caption slot only, no new band).

## Flow
- route handler -> runJob('practice', () => makeItems(...)) -> job start event -> pipeline -> practice.set + job done | job failed
- a second POST of a running kind -> 409, no engine call
- hint -> hint.set (clears lesson) -> runJob('lesson', pick, key) -> lesson.set{key} applied only if key === s.hint.key
- TV Topics / Hint read s.jobs; Select on a failed practice job re-posts

## Expected impact
Every pipeline failure becomes a visible, recoverable state on the TV instead of an eternal wait; the Recap's hint count and the memory prompt stop over-counting; the wrong lesson can no longer open from a new hint; the next route added gets the lifecycle for free instead of a seventh copy.

## Evaluation
Claim: one job runner and a typed jobs record close the silent-failure, double-count and stale-lesson defects the per-route lifecycle causes.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (plus the GUARD, green by design); 21 status dispatches, 6 try/catch copies, 1 route unguarded
After: 8 of 8; one runner, 0 hand-rolled try/catch in the 7 routes
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: architecture

critic.deck_line: Approve: every homework pipeline failure becomes a visible, retryable state on the TV; hint counts and the stale-lesson bug fixed on the way.

cards.title: 'How did you get there?' settles the item: spoken value substituted on the walk
acceptance: case 1: marked sheet (maths-rules-test.cjs:50-57 fixture) with item 4 'x+1=10' unsure; text stub {reply:'Look at the line where the 1 moved.', value:'9', slip:'unclear'}; POST /api/explain {transcript:'I took one away and got nine', n:3} -> session practice.items[3].verdict === 'right', said === 'Number 4 is right.', learner skills['linear-one-step'].seen +1 and right +1; response carries settled:'right' (tools/maths-rules-test.cjs, text stubbed)

case 2: same unsure item, stub value 'x = 11', slip 'sign-lost-moving' -> verdict 'wrong', slip 'sign-lost-moving', said === slip('sign-lost-moving').says, learner slips include it, seen +1 right +0 (tools/maths-rules-test.cjs)

case 3: unsure item, stub value '' or 'about nine' (unreadable by verify's evaluate) -> verdict stays 'unsure', said stays the ASK line, learner record unchanged (no skills write) (tools/maths-rules-test.cjs)

case 4: an item already 'wrong' from marking, explained twice with a value that verifies -> verdict stays 'wrong' and learner seen does not move on either call (a settled item is never re-settled or re-recorded) (tools/maths-rules-test.cjs)

case 5: stub reply that leaks the solution for 'x-5=2' ('You should get 7.' or 'so x = 7') -> the reply the route returns and the one the session carries contain no number that verify() accepts for the question; the ASK line stands in (tools/maths-rules-test.cjs)

case 6: after an explanation the walk item carries the desk's reply for the TV caption slot (items[n].reply or said), and the reply is no longer only a status line (tools/maths-rules-test.cjs, reads getSession())

GUARD: case 7: every said/reply on every item after settling carries no value other than the item number (the check at maths-rules-test.cjs:70 extended to settled items), and keysIn(session.practice) never includes 'answer' or 'solution' (maths-rules-test.cjs:126-134 pattern)
premise: desk/src/lib/desk/mark.ts:47,91-93 - an item where the marker and substitution disagree becomes 'unsure' and says 'I got something different for number n. How did you get there?'

desk/src/lib/desk/mark.ts:91 - three independent routes to unsure (no model solution, model solution fails verify, model verdict disagrees with substitution); the suite's fixture lands 3 of 6 items there (tools/maths-rules-test.cjs:61)
desk/src/lib/desk/mark.ts:104 - recordAttempt runs only for settled items; an unsure item never reaches the learner record (tools/maths-rules-test.cjs:75 pins it)
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:276-296 - the phone offers 'Tell the desk how you got it' exactly on wrong and unsure walk items
desk/src/app/api/explain/route.ts:17-18 - the reply goes to dispatch status and back to the phone; nothing on the practice item changes and no learner write happens
desk/src/app/tv/page.tsx:201 - status renders only in the bench bar, so the TV walk (the screen the phone says to look at, page.tsx:279) never shows the reply
desk/src/lib/desk/explain.ts:46-50 - a closed-vocabulary slip is computed and returned; desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:166-167 reads only j.reply, so 0 consumers use the slip
desk/src/lib/desk/explain.ts:14-18 - the schema has no field for the value the student says they got, so the one thing verify() can check is never asked for
desk/src/lib/desk/explain.ts:49 - the reply is only trimmed; withholding rests on the prompt at :31 though verify() could check it
desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:177 - practice.marked is the only event that writes verdicts; there is no per-item settle
desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:779,809 - an unsure item reads 'The desk is not sure' and its caption is the ASK line, for the rest of the walk
cards.rollback: Three commits (settle() + leak check in rules/maths + mark.ts reusing it; explain value field + route + practice.settle event; Walk caption + phone line) revert in reverse; the new event and the optional item field are additive, older session.json loads through shown() unchanged, and mark.ts behaviour is pinned by the existing marking tests at every step.
cards.runner_up: Essay compare mode: re-reading a revised paragraph through the same lens shows which faulty sentences were fixed, not just the latest reading (analyseEssay keeps no previous analysis, essay.ts:51, store.ts:165).
cards.body:
## Summary
On the marked walk the desk says 'How did you get there?' on every unsure item, the learner holds the phone button and explains - and nothing on the TV, the item or the record changes. Make that explanation settle the item: the model transcribes the value the learner says they got (evidence), verify() substitutes it (truth), and the unsure item becomes Right or Look again on the TV, with the attempt recorded once.

## Description
Unsure is a designed silence (docs/STUDY-DESK-SCOPE.md 'Silence is a designed state'), but today it is a dead end. The learner answers the desk's question by voice; explain.ts computes a reply and a closed-vocabulary slip; the route drops the slip and writes the reply to a status line the TV stage never renders; the item keeps 'The desk is not sure' and the learner record never hears about it. Most unsure items are handwriting the vision model misread, and a spoken value is a second, independent reading of exactly what was lost.

The settle rule is lifted out of mark.ts:85-105 into one function in rules/maths.ts that both marking and explanation call: substitute the learner's value, 'right' or 'wrong' by verify, keep a slip only on a wrong item and only from the topic's vocabulary, build `said` from code (RIGHT(n) or the slip's says), never a value. explain.ts adds a `value` field to its schema; the route settles an unsure item through that rule, records one attempt, and dispatches a per-item `practice.settle` event. A settled item is never re-settled. The model reply is checked by the same rules module: any number in it that verify() accepts for the question is a leak and the reply is replaced by the ASK line. The reply then rides on the item so the Walk shows it in the caption slot (On Air: prose only in the caption), and the phone shows the same reply plus 'the TV has it'.

Decisions stay in code: the model never decides right or wrong (its prompt still forbids saying so); verify() does. Withholding holds: the verdict word appears only after the learner's own value is substituted, exactly as marking already does. Contract: /api/explain response gains `settled`; session gains the `practice.settle` event and an optional item `reply`. Consumers: desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:161-170, desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:780-813 (Walk), store reduce(); learners.json shape unchanged (recordAttempt as today). TV surface changes, so the overlay's Playwright capture applies.

## Flow
- walk on unsure item n -> phone hold -> transcript -> POST /api/explain {transcript, n}
- explain(): model returns reply, slip, value -> leak check on reply -> settle(item, value, slip) in rules/maths
- unsure + readable value -> practice.settle {n, verdict, slip, said, reply} -> recordAttempt once -> TV walk flips, ticker recounts
- unsure + unreadable value, or an item already settled -> reply only, no record write

## Expected impact
The question the desk asks on every unsure item finally has a consequence the learner sees on the big screen; unsure items stop being lost evidence for the skill estimate and the secure flag; the slip a learner names in their own words reaches the mistake journal; and a model reply that leaks the answer is stopped by code, not by prompt wording.

## Evaluation
Claim: a spoken explanation settles an unsure item by substitution and reaches the TV and the learner record, with withholding checked in code.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (plus the GUARD, green by design); explain's slip has 0 consumers; the reply reaches 0 TV stage elements
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract

critic.deck_line: Approve: an unsure item finally settles from the learner's own spoken value, decided by verify() not the model, with a code check that no reply leaks the answer.
